categories.name: State Dynamics
categories.description: How states of focus or engagement are entered, maintained, exited, and re-entered.

dimensions.name: Entry Threshold
dimensions.short: Cost to start a task once disengaged
dimensions.description: How difficult it is to begin a task when not already engaged. A high score means starting feels effortful, delayed, or requires strong motivation or structure; a low score means tasks can be begun easily and spontaneously.

dimensions.name: Maintenance Robustness
dimensions.description: How stable focus or engagement is once started. A high score means engagement can be sustained for long periods despite distractions; a low score means engagement fades quickly or needs frequent reinforcement.

dimensions.name: Exit Sensitivity
dimensions.short: How easily a state collapses when disturbed
dimensions.description: How sensitive engagement is to interruptions or disruptions. A high score means even small interruptions can break focus; a low score means engagement remains active despite disturbances.

dimensions.name: Re-Entry Cost
dimensions.description: How difficult it is to return to a task after interruption. A high score means resuming feels almost like starting over; a low score means the prior thread can be resumed with little additional effort.

categories.name: Process & Attention Architecture
categories.description: What happens inside an active state.

dimensions.name: Input Gate Tightness
dimensions.short: How selective attention is once engaged
dimensions.description: How strongly incoming information is filtered while focused. A high score means irrelevant input is blocked effectively; a low score means many stimuli enter awareness at once.

dimensions.name: Mode Integrity
dimensions.description: How well one coherent mode of thinking or working is maintained. A high score means mental coherence is well maintained; a low score means attention more often drifts or fragments.

dimensions.name: State Friction
dimensions.short: Cost of switching between tasks or modes
dimensions.description: How effortful it is to change tasks, topics, or mental modes. A high score means switching is disruptive and expensive; a low score means transitions are relatively smooth.

dimensions.name: Baseline Charge
dimensions.description: Natural energy or activation level while working. A high score means strong internal drive or intensity; a low score means a calmer, lower-energy working style.

categories.name: Meaning, Drive & Protection
categories.description: Why engagement happens and why it stops.

dimensions.name: Complexity Drive
dimensions.description: How strongly one is drawn to complexity, structure, and systemic understanding. A high score means deeper patterns and frameworks are naturally sought; a low score means simpler or more concrete tasks are preferred.

dimensions.name: Precision Hunger
dimensions.short: Tension from unresolved structure or errors
dimensions.description: How much discomfort is produced by mistakes, inconsistencies, or unfinished structures. A high score means strong pressure to resolve them; a low score means ambiguity or imperfection is more easily tolerated.

dimensions.name: Resonance Strength
dimensions.short: How strongly meaningful input amplifies engagement
dimensions.description: How powerfully meaningful topics or ideas activate engagement. A high score means interest can strongly increase focus and energy; a low score means meaning has a weaker activating effect.

dimensions.name: Protection Activation
dimensions.description: How quickly disengagement or withdrawal occurs when overwhelmed, stressed, or threatened. A high score means rapid protective withdrawal; a low score means engagement tends to continue longer under strain.

categories.name: Time Dynamics & Recovery
categories.description: How load and disruption unfold over time.

dimensions.name: Temporal Depth
dimensions.description: How far into the future thinking naturally extends. A high score means long-term planning and foresight; a low score means focus is more immediate or short-term.

dimensions.name: Disruption Half-Life
dimensions.short: How long disruptions continue to affect the system
dimensions.description: How long the effects of an interruption or disturbance linger. A high score means disruptions echo for a long time; a low score means their effects dissipate quickly.

dimensions.name: Recovery Demand
dimensions.short: Amount of recovery needed after sustained effort
dimensions.description: How much rest or downtime is needed after prolonged engagement. A high score means significant recovery is required; a low score means recovery is relatively quick.

dimensions.name: Continuity Carrying
dimensions.short: Ability to resume threads after interruption
dimensions.description: How well mental continuity is retained across breaks. A high score means complex threads can be resumed easily; a low score means continuity is more often lost.

categories.name: Coupling Load
categories.description: Cost of aligning with external people, demands, and environments.

dimensions.name: Coupling Load — Social
dimensions.description: How costly social interaction and coordination feel. A high score means group interaction is draining; a low score means it is relatively neutral or energizing.

dimensions.name: Coupling Load — Cognitive
dimensions.description: The cost of handling multiple ideas, tasks, or complex reasoning simultaneously. A high score means cognitive load accumulates quickly; a low score means complexity is more manageable.

dimensions.name: Coupling Load — Sensory
dimensions.description: The cost of sensory-rich environments. A high score means sensory input is draining; a low score means it is more easily tolerated or may be helpful.

dimensions.name: Coupling Load — Affective
dimensions.description: The cost of emotional engagement with others. A high score means emotional labor is draining; a low score means it is more sustainable or energizing.

categories.name: Feedback Sensitivity
categories.description: What kinds of feedback have the strongest effect.

dimensions.name: Social Feedback Sensitivity
dimensions.description: How strongly social feedback affects emotion or motivation. A high score means praise or criticism has strong impact; a low score means external social feedback has less effect.

dimensions.name: Internal Feedback Sensitivity
dimensions.description: How strongly internal standards, values, or perceived correctness guide behavior. A high score means internal coherence is highly motivating; a low score means these internal signals are quieter.

categories.name: Integration Coherence
categories.description: How ideas and internal experience are integrated.

dimensions.name: Conceptual Integration
dimensions.description: How easily complex ideas are integrated into coherent mental models. A high score means strong conceptual synthesis; a low score means ideas remain more fragmented.

dimensions.name: Affective Integration
dimensions.description: How easily feelings are identified, labeled, and articulated. A high score means emotions are clearer and more nameable; a low score means feelings may be present but harder to describe.

categories.name: Sustainability & Context
categories.description: How long regulation holds under load and how context-dependent functioning is.

dimensions.name: Regulation Sustainability
dimensions.short: How long regulation holds under load
dimensions.description: How long self-regulation can be maintained during sustained demands. A high score means regulation can be held for longer; a low score means depletion builds more quickly.

dimensions.name: Context Gating
dimensions.short: How dependent engagement is on specific contexts
dimensions.description: How much functioning depends on the right context. A high score means alignment is crucial; a low score means functioning is more similar across contexts.
